drivers.caveat: Correlation shows how closely two things move together, not cause and effect. Because the AQI is calculated from pollutant concentrations, part of the link between pollutants and the AQI comes from how the AQI is defined.
drivers.findings.heading: What this means
drivers.findings.pm: Fine particles (PM2.5) track the AQI most closely (ρ = {pm25_same} on the same day and {pm25_next} for the next day), followed by PM10 ({pm10_same}) and ozone ({o3_same}). PM2.5 is the pollutant to prioritise.
drivers.findings.rain: Rain helps clean the air: the longer it rains, the lower the AQI (ρ = {rain_same} on the same day and {rain_next} for the next day).
drivers.findings.wind: Wind mainly disperses combustion gases: wind speed correlates {wind_no2} with NO₂ and {wind_co} with CO, although its direct link to the AQI is weak.
drivers.findings.persistence: Today's AQI strongly predicts tomorrow's (ρ = {persistence}), so poor conditions tend to last several days.
drivers.findings.model: The forecast model relies most on: {top1}; {top2}; and {top3}.
drivers.findings.warning: Early-warning signal: watch for {dry_days} or more days in a row without rain combined with weak wind (below {wind_kmh} km/h), especially when the forecast approaches AQI {threshold}.
drivers.correlation.heading: How pollutants and weather relate to the AQI
drivers.correlation.caption: ρ (Spearman correlation) ranges from −1 to 1. The further from 0, the stronger the link. Red means it moves with the AQI, blue means it moves against it.
drivers.correlation.table: Show all correlation values as a table

forecast.advisory.none: No advisory. The forecast and its P90 upper band for days 1 to {actionable_days} stay below AQI {threshold} (highest upper band: {max_high}).
forecast.advisory.tier1: Tier 1 advisory: the forecast or its P90 upper band exceeds AQI {threshold} on day {days}. Consider a public health advisory once an analyst confirms it.
forecast.advisory.tier2: Tier 2 advisory: the forecast or its P90 upper band exceeds AQI {threshold} on day {days}, and the weather is dry with weak wind. Consider raising the alert level once an analyst confirms it.
forecast.advisory.conditions: Tier 2 conditions as of {date}: wettest day in the last {dry_days} days {rain} mm (required: under {no_rain} mm each day) – {dry_status}; maximum wind {wind} km/h (required: under {calm} km/h) – {calm_status}.

advice.moderate.sensitive: If you are unusually sensitive to air pollution, consider making outdoor activities shorter and less intense. Go inside if you have symptoms such as coughing or shortness of breath.

advice.source: Advice source: US EPA, Technical Assistance Document for the Reporting of Daily Air Quality – the Air Quality Index (AQI), May 2026, Tables 4–5 (particle pollution).
glossary.heading: What these terms mean
glossary.us_aqi: **US AQI**: the US EPA air quality index, on a scale from {low} to above {high}; the higher the number, the worse the air. The US AQI differs from Indonesia's official ISPU index, so their numbers cannot be compared directly.
glossary.range: **Likely range (P10–P90)**: based on past forecast errors, the actual value fell between this lower and upper bound about {share} times out of 10. It is an estimate, not a guarantee.
glossary.outlook: **Forecast and outlook**: days {first} to {last} are reliable enough to support advisories. Days {outlook_first} to {horizon} are only a rough outlook, because the model's accuracy drops after day {last}.
glossary.sensitive: **Sensitive groups**: people more easily affected by particle pollution: people with heart or lung disease, older adults, and children and teenagers (US EPA).
glossary.pm25: **PM2.5 (fine particles)**: particles in the air {size} micrometres across or smaller, small enough to reach deep into the lungs. In Denpasar, PM2.5 drives the AQI most.
glossary.who: **WHO guideline**: the WHO ({year}) recommends that daily mean PM2.5 stay at or below {limit} µg/m³. Exceeding the guideline does not necessarily put the air in an unhealthy AQI category.
glossary.rolling: **{days}-day rolling mean**: the average AQI over the {days} days around each date. It smooths out day-to-day swings so the long-term trend is easier to see.
glossary.cams: **CAMS**: the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service, the atmosphere monitoring service of the European Union's Copernicus programme. The air quality data in this dashboard are CAMS model estimates, not ground-station measurements. When the CAMS model is upgraded, pollutant levels can shift.
glossary.spearman: **Spearman correlation (ρ)**: how consistently two things rise and fall together, from {min} (always opposite) to {max} (always together). Values near {zero} mean there is no consistent link. Correlation does not prove cause and effect.
glossary.importance: **RMSE increase**: RMSE is the typical size of the forecast error, in AQI points. If shuffling one variable makes the error grow a lot, the model relies heavily on that variable.
glossary.tiers: **Tier 1 and Tier 2 advisories**: Tier 1 applies when the forecast or its upper band exceeds AQI {threshold} within the next {days} days. Tier 2 applies when Tier 1 coincides with dry weather and weak wind, conditions that let pollution linger.
sidebar.sources: Data: {cams} model estimates, compiled in the Kaggle datasets {aq} and {weather}. Scale: {epa}. Guideline: {who}.

reliability.heading: How reliable is this forecast?
reliability.caption: Tested on {start} to {end}, a period not used to train the model.
reliability.summary: For days 1 to {last}, the forecast category was right about {near_low}–{near_high} of the time. From day {first_outlook}, it drops to about {far_low}–{far_high}.
reliability.b3: Category accuracy above the best benchmark: {model} vs. {bench}.
reliability.d4: RMSE and MAE below both benchmarks: RMSE {rmse} vs. {bench_rmse}, MAE {mae} vs. {bench_mae}.
reliability.d5: Mean sMAPE of at most {target}: the result is {smape}. The target is met only for day 1 ({day1}).
reliability.benchmark_line: Dashed horizontal line: accuracy of the best benchmark (persistence), {value}.
reliability.benchmark_table: The model compared with two simple forecasts (mean over {horizon} days)
reliability.rmse_heading: Forecast error by day (lower is better)
reliability.regime_heading: Error before and after the CAMS 50r1 model update
reliability.regime_caption: Test-period RMSE before and after {date}. Errors are much smaller after the update, so current reliability may look better than the test-period average.
reliability.avp_heading: Observed and forecast AQI over the test period
glossary.accuracy: **Category accuracy**: how often the forecast falls in the same US AQI category as what actually happened (for example both "Moderate"). This matters most for advisory decisions.
glossary.rmse: **RMSE**: the typical size of the forecast error in AQI points, weighting large errors more. Lower is better.
glossary.mae: **MAE**: the average difference between forecast and actual value, in AQI points. Lower is better.
glossary.smape: **sMAPE**: the average error as a percentage of the actual value, so days can be compared easily. Lower is better.
glossary.benchmarks: **Benchmarks (persistence and climatology)**: the two simplest forecasts, assuming tomorrow equals today, or using that month's average. The model is useful only if it beats both.
about.intro.heading: About this dashboard
about.intro.body: This dashboard helps the environment agencies, health services, tourism operators, and the public understand Denpasar's air quality through three tools:
about.intro.tool1: **A baseline**: when air quality risk is highest (Overview page).
about.intro.tool2: **Key factors**: the pollutant and weather conditions behind high-AQI days (Key Factors page).
about.intro.tool3: **A {horizon}-day forecast**: so advisories can be prepared before air quality deteriorates ({horizon}-Day Forecast page).
about.data.heading: Data
about.data.period: Denpasar only, daily data from {start} to {end} ({days} days).
about.data.estimates: Air quality values are **model estimates** from the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS), not ground-station measurements. Studies of CAMS report persistent differences from surface measurements, especially for PM2.5.
about.data.version: Data version: `{version}`. It confirms that all figures come from the same notebook export.
about.cams.heading: CAMS model updates
about.cams.why: Each time the CAMS model is updated, some pollutant levels can shift even though the air itself has not changed. Sudden changes around an update date should therefore be read with care.
about.aqi.heading: How to read the US AQI
about.aqi.body: The US AQI turns pollutant concentrations into a single number. The higher the number, the worse the air. In this dashboard, every category is always shown with both its colour and its name.
about.aqi.meaning.good: Air quality is satisfactory, and air pollution poses little or no risk.
about.aqi.meaning.moderate: Air quality is acceptable, but there may be a risk for some people who are unusually sensitive to air pollution.
about.aqi.meaning.unhealthy_for_sensitiv: Members of sensitive groups may experience health effects; the general public is less likely to be affected.
about.aqi.meaning.unhealthy: Some members of the general public may experience health effects; sensitive groups may experience more serious effects.
about.aqi.meaning.very_unhealthy: Health alert: the risk of health effects is increased for everyone.
about.aqi.meaning.hazardous: Health warning of emergency conditions: everyone is more likely to be affected.
about.aqi.source: Source of the category descriptions: US EPA, AirNow – AQI Basics.
about.aqi.ispu: The US AQI is not ISPU (Indeks Standar Pencemar Udara), the index used by the Indonesian government. The category names are similar but the thresholds differ, so a US AQI value cannot be read as an ISPU value.
about.model.heading: The forecast model
about.model.what: A Random Forest model that forecasts the AQI for the next {horizon} days at once, from {features} variables observed up to the last day of data: recent AQI, pollutants, weather, and seasonal patterns.
about.model.refit: After evaluation, the model was retrained on {rows} days of data ({start} to {end}) so that it reflects the latest conditions.
about.model.trees: Main settings: {trees} decision trees, a maximum depth of {depth}, and at least {leaf} days in every leaf.
about.model.band: The P10–P90 range on the forecast comes from the model's errors on the test period: for each forecast day, the P10 and P90 percentiles of those errors are added to the forecast value.
about.use.heading: Conditions of use
about.use.days: This forecast is supervised decision support. Days 1 to {last} can support advisories; days {first_outlook} to {horizon} are an outlook only.
about.use.human: An analyst at the health service or DLH confirms every advisory before it is published.
about.use.retrain: The model should be retrained regularly, at least monthly and after every CAMS model update, while its category accuracy is monitored.
about.use.tiers: Advisory rule: Tier 1 when the forecast or its P90 upper band exceeds AQI {threshold} within the next {days} days; Tier 2 when this happens during dry weather with weak wind.
about.glossary.heading: Glossary
about.limits.heading: Limitations
about.limits.model_data: **Model-based data**: CAMS estimates can shift when the model is updated and differ from surface measurements. A step in SO₂ in {year} remains unexplained.
about.limits.history: **Short history**: the data cover only about {years} years, so seasonal patterns cannot be learned robustly yet.
about.limits.weather: **No weather forecasts**: the model uses only weather that has already happened, not forecasts for the coming days, so longer-range forecasts drift towards the seasonal average.
about.limits.extremes: **Few extreme days**: only {days} days had an AQI above {threshold}, so the model tends to underestimate pollution spikes.
about.limits.drivers: **Scope of factors**: traffic, tourist arrivals, and waste-burning reports are not included, so pollution sources cannot yet be separated.
about.limits.band: **Empirical uncertainty range**: the P10–P90 range is estimated from the model before retraining, so it approximates, but does not guarantee, the final model's coverage.
